tr.text: Offering an oblation in the fire saying, ‘Svaha to fire’, he drips the remnant adhering to the ladle into the paste. Offering and oblation saying, ‘Svaha to the moon,’ he drips, etc. Offering an oblation saying, ‘Svaha to the earth’, he drips, etc. Offering an oblation saying, ‘Svaha to the sky’, he drips, etc. Offering an oblation saying, ‘Svaha to heaven’, he drips, etc. Offering an oblation saying, ‘Svaha to the earth, sky and heaven’, he drips, etc. Offering an oblation saying, ‘Svaha to the Brahmana’, he drips, etc. Offering an oblation saying, ‘Svaha to the Kshatriya’, he drips, etc. Offering an oblation saying, ‘Svaha to the past’, he drips, etc. Offering an oblation saying, ‘Svaha to the future’, he drips, etc. Offering an oblation saying, ‘Svaha to the whole’, he drips, etc. Offering an oblation saying, ‘Svaha to all’, he drips, etc. Offering an oblation saying, ‘Svaha to Prajapati’, he drips, etc.

Then he touches the paste saying, ‘You move (as the vital force), you burn (as fire), you are infinite (as Brahman), you are still (as the sky). You combine everything in yourself. You are the sound ‘Him’, and are uttered as ‘Him’ (in the sacrifice by the Prastotr). You are the Udgitha and are chanted (by the Udgatr). You are recited (by the Adhvaryu) and recited back (by the Agnidhra). You are fully ablaze in a humid (cloud). You are omnipresent, and master. You are food (as the moon), and light (as fire). You are death, and you are that in which all things merge’.

sa: अथैनम् उद्यच्छत्य् आमंस्य् आमं हि ते महि ।
स मां राजेशनो ऽधिपतिं करोत्व् इति ॥
iast: athainam udyacchaty āmaṃsy āmaṃ hi te mahi ।

tr.text: Then he takes it up saying, ‘You know all (as the vital force); we too are aware of your greatness. The vital force is the king, the lord, the ruler. May it make me king, lord and ruler !’

sa: मधु वाता ऋतायते मधु क्षरन्ति सिन्धवः ।
मधु नक्तम् उतोषसो मधुमत् पार्थिवं रजः ।
मधुमान् नो वनस्पतिर् मधुमां अस्तु सूर्यः ।
सर्वाश् च मधुमतीर् अहम् एवेदं सर्वं भूयासं भूर् भुवः स्वः स्वाहेति अन्तत आचम्य पाणी प्रक्षाल्य जघनेनाग्निं प्राक्शिराः संविशति ।
यथेतम् एत्य जघनेनाग्निम् आसीनो वंशं जपति ॥
iast: madhu vātā ṛtāyate madhu kṣaranti sindhavaḥ ।
madhu naktam utoṣaso madhumat pārthivaṃ rajaḥ ।
madhumān no vanaspatir madhumāṃ astu sūryaḥ ।
sarvāś ca madhumatīr aham evedaṃ sarvaṃ bhūyāsaṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāheti antata ācamya pāṇī prakṣālya jaghanenāgniṃ prākśirāḥ saṃviśati ।
yathetam etya jaghanenāgnim āsīno vaṃśaṃ japati ॥
words: the sphere of vapour or mist
hail! hail to! may a blessing rest on!
to sip (water) from the palm of the hand for purification
name of seven deities of the heavenly sphere
to stand or place one's self near
the bamboo cane or any cane (also "sugarcane" and "Shorea Robusta")
to utter in a low voice

tr.text: Then he drinks it saying, ‘The radiant sun is adorable --; The winds are blowing sweetly, the rivers are shedding honey, may the herbs be sweet unto us ! Svaha to the earth. Glory we meditate upon; May the nights and days be charming, and the dust of the earth be sweet, may heaven, our father, be gracious ! Svaha to the sky. May he direct our intellect; May the Soma creeper be sweet unto us, may the sun be kind, may the quarters be helpful to us ! Svaha to heaven’. Then he repeats the whole Gayatri and the whole Madhumati, and says at the end, ‘May I be all this ! Svaha to the earth, sky and heaven.’ Then he drinks the whole remnant, washes his hands, and lies behind the fire with his head to the east. In the morning he salutes the sun saying, ‘Thou art the one lotus of the quarters; may I be the one lotus of men !’ Then he returns the way he went, sits behind the fire, and repeats the line of teachers.

sa: तं हैतम् उद्दालक आरुणिर् वाजसनेयाय याज्ञवल्क्यायान्तेवासिन उक्त्वोवाच -- अपि य एनं शुष्के स्थाणौ निषिञ्चेज् जायेरञ् छाखाः प्ररोहेयुः पलाशानीति ॥
iast: taṃ haitam uddālaka āruṇir vājasaneyāya yājñavalkyāyāntevāsina uktvovāca -- api ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcej jāyerañ chākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti ॥
words: name of Uddālaka (a renowned Brāhmaṇa teacher)
a pupil who dwells near or in the house of his teacher

tr.text: Uddalaka, the son of Aruni, taught this to his pupil Yajnavalkya, the Vajasaneya, and said, ‘Should one sprinkle it even on a dry stump, branches would grow and leaves sprout’.

sa: एतम् उ हैव वाजसनेयो याज्नवल्क्यो मधुकाय पैङ्ग्यायान्तेवासिन उक्त्वोवाच -- अपि य एनं शुष्के स्थाणौ निषिञ्चेज् जायेरञ् छाखाः प्ररोहेयुः पलाशानीति ॥
iast: etam u haiva vājasaneyo yājnavalkyo madhukāya paiṅgyāyāntevāsina uktvovāca -- api ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcej jāyerañ chākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti ॥

tr.text: The Yajnavalkya, the Vajasaneya, taught this to his pupil Madhuka, the son of Paingi and said, ‘Should one sprinkle it even on a dry stump, branches would grow and leaves sprout’.

sa: एतम् उ हैव मधुकः पैङ्ग्यश् चूलाय भागवित्तये ऽन्तेवासिन उक्त्वोवाच -- अपि य एनं शुष्के स्थाणौ निषिञ्चेज् जायेरञ् छाखाः प्ररोहेयुः पलाशानीति ॥
iast: etam u haiva madhukaḥ paiṅgyaś cūlāya bhāgavittaye ’ntevāsina uktvovāca -- api ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcej jāyerañ chākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti ॥
words: a pupil who dwells near or in the house of his teacher

tr.text: Madhuka, the son of Paingi, again taught this to his pupil Cula, the son of Bhagavitta, and said, ‘Should one sprinkle it even on a dry stump, branches would grow and leaves sprout’.

sa: एतम् उ हैव चूलो भागवित्तिर् जानकय आयःस्थूणायान्तेवासिन उक्त्वोवाच -- अपि य एनं शुष्के स्थाणौ निषिञ्चेज् जायेरञ् छाखाः प्ररोहेयुः पलाशानीति ॥
iast: etam u haiva cūlo bhāgavittir jānakaya āyaḥsthūṇāyāntevāsina uktvovāca -- api ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcej jāyerañ chākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti ॥
words: a pupil who dwells near or in the house of his teacher

tr.text: Then Cula, the son of Bhagavitta, taught this to his pupil Janaki, the son of Ayasthuna, and said, ‘Should one sprinkle it even on a dry stump, branches would grow and leaves sprout’.

sa: एतम् उ हैव जानकिर् आयस्थूणः सत्यकामाय जाबालायान्तेवासिन उक्त्वोवाच -- अपि य एनं शुष्के स्थाणौ निषिञ्चेज् जायेरञ् छाखाः प्ररोहेयुः पलाशानीति ॥
iast: etam u haiva jānakir āyasthūṇaḥ satyakāmāya jābālāyāntevāsina uktvovāca -- api ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcej jāyerañ chākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti ॥

tr.text: Janaki, the son of Ayasthuna, again taught this to Satyakama, the son of Jabala, and said, ‘Should one sprinkle it even on a dry stump, branches would grow and leaves sprout’.

sa: एतम् उ हैव सत्यकामो जाबालो ऽन्तेवासिभ्य उक्त्वोव -- अचापि य एनं शुष्के स्थाणौ निषिञ्चेज् जायेरञ् छाखाः प्ररोहेयुः पलाशानीति ।
तम् एतं नापुत्राय वानन्तेवासिने वा ब्रूयात् ॥
iast: etam u haiva satyakāmo jābālo ’ntevāsibhya uktvova -- acāpi ya enaṃ śuṣke sthāṇau niṣiñcej jāyerañ chākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśānīti ।
tam etaṃ nāputrāya vānantevāsine vā brūyāt ॥
words: a pupil who dwells near or in the house of his teacher

tr.text: And Satyakama, the son of Jabala, in his turn, taught this to his pupils and said, ‘Should one sprinkle it even on a dry stump, branches would grow and leaves sprout’. One must not teach this to anyone but a son or a pupil.

sa: औदुम्बरः स्रुव औदुम्बरश् चमस औदुम्बर इध्म औदुम्बर्या उपमन्थन्यौ ।
व्रीहियवास् तिलमाषा अणुप्रियंगवो गोधूमाश् च मसूराश् च खल्वाश् च खलकुलाश् च ।
तान् पिष्टान् दधनि मधुनि घृत उपसिञ्चति ।
iast: audumbaraḥ sruva audumbaraś camasa audumbara idhma audumbaryā upamanthanyau ।
vrīhiyavās tilamāṣā aṇupriyaṃgavo godhūmāś ca masūrāś ca khalvāś ca khalakulāś ca ।
tān piṣṭān dadhani madhuni ghṛta upasiñcati ।
words: coming from the tree Udumbara or Ficus Religiosa
coming from the tree Udumbara or Ficus Religiosa
a vessel used at sacrifices for drinking the Soma
coming from the tree Udumbara or Ficus Religiosa
coming from the tree Udumbara or Ficus Religiosa
used or produced in a village
Sesamum indicum DC. (its blossom is compared to the nose)
a kind of grain or leguminous plant

tr.text: Four things are made of fig wood: the ladle, the bowl, the fuel and the two mixing rods. The cultivated grains are ten in number: Rice, barley, sesame, beans, Anu, Priyangu, wheat, lentils, pulse and vetches. They should be crushed and soaked in curds, honey and clarified butter, and offered as an oblation.
The earth is the essence of all these beings, water the essence of the earth, herbs of water, flowers of herbs, fruits of flowers, man of fruits, and the seed of man.

sa: स ह प्रजापतिर् ईक्षां चक्रे -- हन्तास्मै प्रतिष्ठां कल्पयानीति स स्त्रियं ससृजे ।
स एतं प्राञ्चं ग्रावाणम् आत्मन एव समुदपारयत् ।
iast: sa ha prajāpatir īkṣāṃ cakre -- hantāsmai pratiṣṭhāṃ kalpayānīti sa striyaṃ sasṛje ।
sa etaṃ prāñcaṃ grāvāṇam ātmana eva samudapārayat ।

tr.text: Prajapati thought, ‘Well, let me make an abode for it’, and he created woman.

sa: स यावान् ह वै वाजपेयेन यजमनस्य लोको भवति तावान् अस्य लोको भवति ।
य एवं विद्वान् अधोपहासं चरत्य् आसां स्त्रीणां सुकृतं वृङ्क्ते ।
अथ य इदम् अविद्वान् अधोपहासं चरत्य् आस्य स्त्रियः सुकृतं वृञ्जते ॥
iast: sa yāvān ha vai vājapeyena yajamanasya loko bhavati tāvān asya loko bhavati ।
ya evaṃ vidvān adhopahāsaṃ caraty āsāṃ strīṇāṃ sukṛtaṃ vṛṅkte ।
atha ya idam avidvān adhopahāsaṃ caraty āsya striyaḥ sukṛtaṃ vṛñjate ॥

sa: एतद् ध स्म वै तद् विद्वान् उद्दालक आरुनिर् आह ।
एतद् ध स्म वै तद् विद्वान् नाको मौद्गल्य आह ।
एतद् ध स्म वै तद् विद्वान् कुमारहारित आह -- बहवो मर्या ब्राह्मनायना निरिन्द्रिया विसुकृतो ऽस्माल् लोकात् प्रयन्ति य इदम् अविद्वांसो ऽधोपहासं चरन्तीति ।
बहु वा इदं सुप्तस्य वा जाग्रतो वा रेतः स्कन्दति ॥
iast: etad dha sma vai tad vidvān uddālaka ārunir āha ।
etad dha sma vai tad vidvān nāko maudgalya āha ।
etad dha sma vai tad vidvān kumārahārita āha -- bahavo maryā brāhmanāyanā nirindriyā visukṛto ’smāl lokāt prayanti ya idam avidvāṃso ’dhopahāsaṃ carantīti ।
bahu vā idaṃ suptasya vā jāgrato vā retaḥ skandati ॥

tr.text: Knowing verily this, Uddalaka, the son of Aruna, Naka, the son of Mudgala, and Kumaraharita said, ‘Many men -Brahmanas only in name – who have union without knowing as above, depart from this world impotent and bereft of merits’.

sa: तद् अभिमृशेद् अनु वा मन्त्रयेत -- यन् मे ऽद्य रेतः पृथिवीम् अस्कान्त्सीद् यद् ओषधीर् अप्य् असरद् यद् अपः ।
पुनर् माम् ऐतु इन्द्रियं पुनस् तेजः पुनर् भगः ।
इत्य् अनामिकाङ्गुष्ठाभ्याम् आदायान्तरेण स्तनौ वा भ्रुवौ वा निमृज्यात् ॥
iast: tad abhimṛśed anu vā mantrayeta -- yan me ’dya retaḥ pṛthivīm askāntsīd yad oṣadhīr apy asarad yad apaḥ ।
punar mām aitu indriyaṃ punas tejaḥ punar bhagaḥ ।
ity anāmikāṅguṣṭhābhyām ādāyāntareṇa stanau vā bhruvau vā nimṛjyāt ॥

sa: अथ यद्य् उदक आत्मानं पश्येत् तद् अभिमन्त्रयेत -- मयि तेज इन्द्रियं यशो द्रविणं सुकृतम् इति ।
श्रीर् ह वा एषा स्त्रीणां यन् मलोद्वासाः ।
iast: atha yady udaka ātmānaṃ paśyet tad abhimantrayeta -- mayi teja indriyaṃ yaśo draviṇaṃ sukṛtam iti ।
śrīr ha vā eṣā strīṇāṃ yan malodvāsāḥ ।

tr.text: If man sees his reflection in water, he should recite the following Mantra: ‘(May the gods grant) me lustre, manhood, reputation, wealth and merits’. She (his wife) is indeed the goddess of beauty among women. Therefore he should approach this handsome woman and speak to her.

sa: सा चेद् अस्मै न दद्यात् कामम् एनाम् अवक्रिणीयात् ।
सा चेद् अस्मै नैव दद्यात् कामम् एनां यष्ट्या वा पाणिना वोपहत्यातिक्रामेत् ।
इन्द्रियेन ते यशसा यश आदद इति ।
iast: sā ced asmai na dadyāt kāmam enām avakriṇīyāt ।
sā ced asmai naiva dadyāt kāmam enāṃ yaṣṭyā vā pāṇinā vopahatyātikrāmet ।
indriyena te yaśasā yaśa ādada iti ।

tr.text: If she is not willing, he should buy her over; and if she is still unyielding, he should strike her with a stick or with the hand and proceed, uttering the following Mantra, 'I take away your reputation’, etc. She is then actually discarded.

sa: सा चेद् अस्मै दद्याद् इन्द्रियेण ते यशसा यश आदधामीति ।
iast: sā ced asmai dadyād indriyeṇa te yaśasā yaśa ādadhāmīti ।

tr.text: If she is willing, he should proceed, uttering the following Mantra: ‘I transmit reputation into you’, and they both become reputed.

sa: स याम् इच्छेत् -- कामयेत मेति तस्याम् अर्थं निष्ठाय मुखेन मुखं संधायोपस्थम् अस्या अभिमृश्य जपेत् --
स त्वम् अङ्गकषायो ऽसि दिग्धविद्धाम् इव मादयेमाम् अमूं मयीति ॥
iast: sa yām icchet -- kāmayeta meti tasyām arthaṃ niṣṭhāya mukhena mukhaṃ saṃdhāyopastham asyā abhimṛśya japet --
sa tvam aṅgakaṣāyo ’si digdhaviddhām iva mādayemām amūṃ mayīti ॥

sa: अथ याम् इच्छेन् न गर्भं दधीतेति तस्याम् अर्थं निष्ठाय मुखेन मुखं संधायाभिप्राण्यापान्यात् ।
इन्द्रियेण ते रेतसा रेत आदद इति ।
iast: atha yām icchen na garbhaṃ dadhīteti tasyām arthaṃ niṣṭhāya mukhena mukhaṃ saṃdhāyābhiprāṇyāpānyāt ।
indriyeṇa te retasā reta ādada iti ।

sa: अथ याम् इच्छेद् दधीतेति तस्याम् अर्थं निष्ठाय मुखेन मुखं संधायापान्याभिप्राण्यात् ।
iast: atha yām icched dadhīteti tasyām arthaṃ niṣṭhāya mukhena mukhaṃ saṃdhāyāpānyābhiprāṇyāt ।

sa: अथ यस्य जायायै जारः स्यात् तं चेद् द्विष्याद् आमपात्रे ऽग्निम् उपसमाधाय प्रतिलोमं शरबर्हिः स्तीर्त्वा तस्मिन्न् एताः शरभृष्टीः प्रतिलोमाः सर्पिषाक्ता जुहुयात् ।
स वा एष निरिन्द्रियो विसुकृतो ऽस्माल् लोकाद् प्रैति यम् एवंविद् ब्राह्मणः शपति ।
iast: atha yasya jāyāyai jāraḥ syāt taṃ ced dviṣyād āmapātre ’gnim upasamādhāya pratilomaṃ śarabarhiḥ stīrtvā tasminn etāḥ śarabhṛṣṭīḥ pratilomāḥ sarpiṣāktā juhuyāt ।
sa vā eṣa nirindriyo visukṛto ’smāl lokād praiti yam evaṃvid brāhmaṇaḥ śapati ।

tr.text: If a man’s wife has a lover whom he wishes to injure, he should put the fire in an unbaked earthen vessel, spread stalks of reed and Kusa grass in an inverse way, and offer the reed tips, soaked in clarified butter, in the fire in an inverse way, saying, ‘Thou hast sacrificed in my kindled fire, I take away thy Prana and Apana – such and such. Thou hast sacrificed in my kindled fire, I take away thy sons and animals – such and such. Thou hast sacrificed in my kindled fire, I take away thy Vedic rites and those done according to the Smriti – such and such. Thou hast sacrificed in my kindled fire, I take away thy hopes and expectations – such and such’. The man whom a Brahmana with knowledge of this ceremony curses, departs from this world emasculated and shorn of his merits. Therefore one should not wish even to cut jokes with the wife of a Vedic scholar who knows this ceremony, for he who has such knowledge becomes an enemy.

sa: अथ यस्य जायाम् आर्तवं विन्देत् त्र्यहं कंसे न पिबेत् ।
iast: atha yasya jāyām ārtavaṃ vindet tryahaṃ kaṃse na pibet ।

tr.text: If anybody’s wife has the monthly sickness, she should drink of three days out of a cup (Kamsa). No Sudra man or woman should touch her. After three nights she should bathe, put on a new cloth, and be put to thresh rice.

sa: स य इच्छेत् -- पुत्रो मे शुक्लो जायेत वेदम् अनुब्रुवीत सर्वम् आयुर् इयाद् इति क्षीरौदनं पाचयित्वा सर्पिष्मन्तम् अश्नीयाताम् ।
iast: sa ya icchet -- putro me śuklo jāyeta vedam anubruvīta sarvam āyur iyād iti kṣīraudanaṃ pācayitvā sarpiṣmantam aśnīyātām ।

tr.text: He who wishes that his son should be born fair, study one Veda and attain a full term of life, should have rice cooked in milk, and he and his wife should eat it with clarified butter. Then they would be able to produce such a son.

sa: अथ य इच्छेत् -- पुत्रो मे कपिलः पिङ्गलो जायेत द्वौ वेदाव् अनुब्रुवीत सर्वम् आयुर् इयाद् इति दध्योदनं पाचयित्वा सर्पिष्मन्तम् अश्नीयाताम् ।
iast: atha ya icchet -- putro me kapilaḥ piṅgalo jāyeta dvau vedāv anubruvīta sarvam āyur iyād iti dadhyodanaṃ pācayitvā sarpiṣmantam aśnīyātām ।

tr.text: He who wishes that his son should be born tawny or brown, study two Vedas and attain a full term of life, should have rice cooked in curd, and he and his wife should eat it with clarified butter. Then they would be able to produce such a son.

sa: अथ य इच्छेत् -- पुत्रो मे श्यामो लोहिताक्षो जायेत त्रीन् वेदान् अनुब्रुवीत सर्वम् आयुर् इयाद् इति उदौदनं पाचयित्वा सर्पिष्मन्तम् अश्नीयाताम् ।
iast: atha ya icchet -- putro me śyāmo lohitākṣo jāyeta trīn vedān anubruvīta sarvam āyur iyād iti udaudanaṃ pācayitvā sarpiṣmantam aśnīyātām ।

tr.text: He who wishes that his son should be born dark with red eyes, study three Vedas and attain a full term of life, should have rice cooked in water and he and his wife should eat with clarified butter. Then they would be able to produce such a son.

sa: अथ य इच्छेद् -- दुहिता मे पण्डिता जायेत सर्वम् आयुर् इयाद् इति तिलौदनं पाचयित्वा सर्पिष्मन्तम् अश्नीयाताम् ।
iast: atha ya icched -- duhitā me paṇḍitā jāyeta sarvam āyur iyād iti tilaudanaṃ pācayitvā sarpiṣmantam aśnīyātām ।

tr.text: He who wishes that a daughter should be born to him who would be a scholar and attain a full term of life, should have rice cooked with sesame, and he and his wife should eat it with clarified butter. Then they would be able to produce such a daughter.

sa: अथ य इच्छेत् -- पुत्रो मे पण्डितो विगीतः समितिंगमः शुश्रूषितां वाचं भाषिता जायेत सर्वान् वेदान् अनुब्रुवीत सर्वम् आयुर् इयाद् इति मांसौदनं पाचयित्वा सर्पिष्मन्तम् अश्नीयाताम् ।
iast: atha ya icchet -- putro me paṇḍito vigītaḥ samitiṃgamaḥ śuśrūṣitāṃ vācaṃ bhāṣitā jāyeta sarvān vedān anubruvīta sarvam āyur iyād iti māṃsaudanaṃ pācayitvā sarpiṣmantam aśnīyātām ।

sa: अथाभिप्रातर् एव स्थालीपाकावृताज्यं चेष्टित्वा स्थालीपाकस्योपघातं जुहोत्य् अग्नये स्वाहानुमतये स्वाहा देवाय सवित्रे सत्यप्रसवाय स्वाहेति ।
प्रक्षाल्य पाणी उदपात्रं पूरयित्वा तेनैनां त्रिर् अभ्युक्षति --
iast: athābhiprātar eva sthālīpākāvṛtājyaṃ ceṣṭitvā sthālīpākasyopaghātaṃ juhoty agnaye svāhānumataye svāhā devāya savitre satyaprasavāya svāheti ।
prakṣālya pāṇī udapātraṃ pūrayitvā tenaināṃ trir abhyukṣati --

tr.text: In the very morning he purifies the clarified butter according to the mode of Sthalipaka, and offers Sthalipaka oblations again and again, saying, ‘Svaha to fire, Svaha to Anumati, Svaha to the radiant sun who produces infallible results’. After offering, he takes up (the remnant of the cooked food), eats part of it and gives the rest to his wife. Then he washes his hands, fills the water-vessel and sprinkles her thrice with that water, saying. ‘Get up from here, Visvavasu, and find out another young woman (who is) with her husband.’

sa: अथैनाम् अभिपद्यते -- अमो ऽहम् अस्मि सा त्वम् ।
ताव् एहि संरभावहै सह रेतो दधावहै ।
iast: athainām abhipadyate -- amo ’ham asmi sā tvam ।
tāv ehi saṃrabhāvahai saha reto dadhāvahai ।
words: to seize or take hold of

tr.text: He embraces her saying, ‘I am the vital force, and you are speech; you are speech, and I am the vital force; I am Saman, and you are Rik; I am heaven, and you are the earth; come, let us strive together so that we may have a male child.’

sa: अथास्या ऊरू विहापयति -- विजिहीथां द्यावापृथिवी इति ।
तस्याम् अर्थं निष्ठाय मुखेन मुखं संधाय त्रिर् एनाम् अनुलोमाम् अनुमार्ष्टि --
विष्णुर् योनिं कल्पयतु त्वष्टा रूपाणि पिंशतु ।
आ सिञ्चतु प्रजापतिर् धाता गर्भं दधातु ते ।
गर्भं धेहि सिनीवालि गर्भं धेहि पृथुष्टुके ।
गर्भं ते अश्विनौ देवाव् आधत्तां पुष्करस्रजौ ॥
iast: athāsyā ūrū vihāpayati -- vijihīthāṃ dyāvāpṛthivī iti ।
tasyām arthaṃ niṣṭhāya mukhena mukhaṃ saṃdhāya trir enām anulomām anumārṣṭi --
viṣṇur yoniṃ kalpayatu tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi piṃśatu ।
ā siñcatu prajāpatir dhātā garbhaṃ dadhātu te ।
garbhaṃ dhehi sinīvāli garbhaṃ dhehi pṛthuṣṭuke ।
garbhaṃ te aśvinau devāv ādhattāṃ puṣkarasrajau ॥
words: name of one of the principal Hindū deities
any outward appearance or phenomenon or colour (often pl.)
having a broad tuft of hair

sa: तं ते गर्भं हवामहे दशमे मासि सूतये ।
यथाग्निगर्भा पृथिवी यथा द्यौर् ऐन्द्रेण गर्भिणी ।
वायुर् दिशां यथा गर्भ एवं गर्भं दधामि ते ऽसाव् इति ॥
iast: taṃ te garbhaṃ havāmahe daśame māsi sūtaye ।
yathāgnigarbhā pṛthivī yathā dyaur aindreṇa garbhiṇī ।
vāyur diśāṃ yathā garbha evaṃ garbhaṃ dadhāmi te ’sāv iti ॥

sa: एवा ते गर्भ एजतु सहावैतु जरायुणा ।
तम् इन्द्र निर्जहि गर्भेण सावरां सहेति ॥
iast: evā te garbha ejatu sahāvaitu jarāyuṇā ।
tam indra nirjahi garbheṇa sāvarāṃ saheti ॥

sa: जाते ऽग्निम् उपसमाधायाङ्क आधाय कंसे पृषदाज्यं संनीय पृषदाज्यस्योपघातं जुहोति --
अस्योपसन्द्यां मा छैत्सीत् प्रजया च पशुभिश् च स्वाहा ।
मयि प्राणांस् त्वयि मनसा जुहोमि स्वाहा ।
यत् कर्मणात्यरीरिचम् यद् वा न्यूनम् इहाकरम् ।
अग्निष्टत् स्विष्टकृद् विद्वान् स्विष्टं सुहुतं करोतु नः स्वाहेति ॥
iast: jāte ’gnim upasamādhāyāṅka ādhāya kaṃse pṛṣadājyaṃ saṃnīya pṛṣadājyasyopaghātaṃ juhoti --
asyopasandyāṃ mā chaitsīt prajayā ca paśubhiś ca svāhā ।
mayi prāṇāṃs tvayi manasā juhomi svāhā ।
yat karmaṇātyarīricam yad vā nyūnam ihākaram ।
agniṣṭat sviṣṭakṛd vidvān sviṣṭaṃ suhutaṃ karotu naḥ svāheti ॥

tr.text: When (the son) is born, he should bring in the fire, take him in his lap, put a mixture of curd and clarified butter in a cup, and offer oblations again and again with that, saying, ‘Growing in this home of mine (as the son), may I maintain a thousand people ! May (the goddess of fortune) never depart with children and animals from his line ! Svaha. The vital force that is in me, I mentally transfer to you. Svaha. If I have done anything too much or to little in this ceremony, may the all-knowing beneficent fire make it just right for me – neither too much nor too little ! Svaha.’

sa: अथास्य दक्षिणं कर्णम् अभिनिधाय वाग् वाग् इति त्रिः ।
अथ दधि मधु घृतं संनीयानन्तर्हितेन जातरूपेण प्राशयति ।
भूस् ते दधामि भुवस् ते दधामि स्वस् ते दधामि भूर् भुवः स्वः सर्वं त्वयि दधामीति ॥
iast: athāsya dakṣiṇaṃ karṇam abhinidhāya vāg vāg iti triḥ ।
atha dadhi madhu ghṛtaṃ saṃnīyānantarhitena jātarūpeṇa prāśayati ।
bhūs te dadhāmi bhuvas te dadhāmi svas te dadhāmi bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ sarvaṃ tvayi dadhāmīti ॥

tr.text: Then putting (his mouth) to the child’s right ear, he should thrice repeat, ‘Speech, speech’. Next mixing curd, honey and clarified butter, he feeds him with (a strip of) gold not obstructed (by anything), saying, ‘I put the earth into you, I put the sky into you, I put heaven into you, I put the whole of the earth, sky and heaven into you’.

sa: तद् अस्यैतद् गुह्यम् एव नाम भवति ॥
iast: tad asyaitad guhyam eva nāma bhavati ॥

tr.text: The he gives him a name, ‘You are Veda (knowledge)’. That is his secret name.

sa: अथैनं मात्रे प्रदाय स्तनं प्रयच्छति -- यस् ते स्तनः शशयो यो मयोभूर् यो रत्नधा वसुविद् यः सुदत्रः ।
येन विश्वा पुष्यसि वार्याणि सरस्वति तम् इह धातवे कर् इति ॥
iast: athainaṃ mātre pradāya stanaṃ prayacchati -- yas te stanaḥ śaśayo yo mayobhūr yo ratnadhā vasuvid yaḥ sudatraḥ ।
yena viśvā puṣyasi vāryāṇi sarasvati tam iha dhātave kar iti ॥
words: the female breast (either human or animal)
a region abounding in pools and lakes

tr.text: Then he hands him to his mother to be suckled, saying, ‘Offering Sarasvati, that breast of thine which is stored with results, is the sustainer of all, full of milk, the obtainer of wealth (one’s deserts) and generous, and through which thou nourishest all who are worthy of it (the gods etc.) – transfer that here (to my wife, for my babe) to suck’.

sa: अथास्य मातरम् अभिमन्त्रयते -- इलासि मैत्रावरुणी वीरे वीरम् अजीजनत् ।
सा त्वं वीरवती भव यास्मान् वीरवतो ऽकरद् इति ।
तं वा एतम् आहुः -- अतिपिता बताभूः ।
परमां बत काष्ठां प्राप श्रिया यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन ।
य एवंविदो ब्राह्मणस्य पुत्रो जायत इति ॥
iast: athāsya mātaram abhimantrayate -- ilāsi maitrāvaruṇī vīre vīram ajījanat ।
sā tvaṃ vīravatī bhava yāsmān vīravato ’karad iti ।
taṃ vā etam āhuḥ -- atipitā batābhūḥ ।
paramāṃ bata kāṣṭhāṃ prāpa śriyā yaśasā brahmavarcasena ।
ya evaṃvido brāhmaṇasya putro jāyata iti ॥

tr.text: Then he addressed the mother: ‘You are the adorable Arundhati, the wife of Vasistha; you have brought forth a male child with the help of me, who am a man. Be the mother of many sons, for you have given us a son’. Of him who is born as the child of a Brahmana with this particular knowledge, they say, ‘You have exceeded your father, and you have exceeded your grandfather. You have reached the extreme limit of attainment through your splendour, fame and Brahmanical power.’

Now the line of teachers: The son of Pautimsa (received it) from the son of Katyayani. He from the son of gautami. The son of Gautami from the son of Bharadvaji. He from the son of Parasari. The son of Parasari from the son of Aupasvasti. He from the son of another Parasari. He from the son of Katyayani. The son of katyayani from the son of Kausiki. The son of Kausiki from the son of Alambi and the son of Vaiyaghrapadi. The son of Vaiyaghrapadi from the son of Kanvi and the son of Kapi. The son of Kapi –

From the son of Atreyi. The son of Atreyi from the son of gautami. The son of Gautami from the son of Bharadvaji. He from the son of parasari. The son of Parasari from the son of Vatsi. The son of Vatsi from the son of another Parasari. The son of Parasari from the son of Varkaruni. He from the son of another Varkaruni. This one from the son of Artabhagi. He from the son of Saungi. The son of Saungi from the son of Samkrti. He from the son of Alambayani. He again from the son of Alambi. The son of Alambi from the son of jayanti. He from the son of Mandukayani. He in his turn from the son of Manduki. The son of manduki from the son of Sandili. The son of Sandili from the son of Rathitari. He from the son of Bhaluki. The son of Bhaluki from the two sons of Kraunciki. They from the son of Vaidabhrti. He from the son of Karsakeyi. He again from the son of Pracinayogi. He from the son of Samjivi. The son of Samjivi from Asurivasin, the son of Prasni. The son of Prasni from Asurayana. He from Asuri. Asuri –

words: a poisonous animal (said to be a kind of mouse)
a poisonous animal (said to be a kind of mouse)
a class of semidivine genii connected with or regulating the course of the sun
a class of semidivine genii connected with or regulating the course of the sun
a class of semidivine genii connected with or regulating the course of the sun
a class of semidivine genii connected with or regulating the course of the sun
a class of semidivine genii connected with or regulating the course of the sun

tr.text: From Yajnavalkya. Yajnavalkya from Uddalaka. Uddalaka from Aruna. Aruna from Upavesi. Upavesi from Kusri. Kusri from Vajasravas. He from Jihvavat, the son of Badhyoga. He from Asita, the son of Varsagana. He from Harita Kasyapa. He from Silpa Kasyapa. This one from Kasyana, the son of Nidhruva. He from Vac. She from Ambhini. She from the sun. These white Yajuses received from the sun are explained by Yajnavalkya Vajasaneya.

words: name of a preceptor and priest with the patr. Kāvaṣeya
name of a preceptor and priest with the patr. Kāvaṣeya

tr.text: The same up to the son of Samjivi. The son of Samjivi from Mandukayani. Mandukayani from mandavya. Mandavya from Kautsa. Kautsa from Mahitthi. He from Vamakaksayana. He from Sandilya. Sandilya from Vatsya. Vatsya from Kusri. Kusri from Yajnavacas, the son of rajastamba. He from Tura, the son of Kavasi. He from Prajapati (Hiranyagarbha). Prajapati through his relation to Brahman (the Vedas). Brahman is self-born. Salutation to Brahman.
